newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end slightly easier after stellar week.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end slightly easier after stellar week.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended slightly easier on Friday as the market underwent some consolidation after a strong run up earlier in the week, brokers said.
"The market needs a period of consolidation," said William Choi, head of Hong Kong sales at SBC Warburg.
The Hang Seng Index slipped 24.07 points to close at 12,218.40. Turnover remained high at HK$7.12 billion, but slightly below Thursday's HK$7.86 billion.
Trading activity was fairly robust for a Friday, even after deducting nearly HK$1.5 billion in trade in Hopewell Holdings and Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) shares.
The Hang Seng Index hit a record closing high of 12,250.57 on Wednesday, and has moved sideways since then. The blue chip index is up 312.89 points on the week.

"Hong Kong has been able to take advantage of the weakness of the region, but we are looking a little rich at this level, Choi said. SBC Warburg has the Hang Seng Index trading on a prospective price earnings ratio of 15 times 1996 earnings.
Chris Sawtell, director technical strategy, at W.I. Carr said the major indices in Hong Kong and New York have hit key levels.
Sawtell said we could see a modest consolidation and then the start of another rally. Or a serious breakdown.
"Any further weakness and I'd go short," said Sawtell.
Not all brokers were so cautious.

"Hong Kong could be at 13,000 sooner rather than later, said James Osborn at ING Barings. "This looks to be the first stage of what could be quite a substantial rally in Hong Kong, that carries us through to 1997, said James Osborn.

Hopewell and its unit CEPA grabbed the market focus on new U.S. energy giant Southern co will buy an 80 percent stake in CEPA in a deal worth HK$21 billion. Total trade in Hopewell amounted to HK$885.8 million and HK$613.04 million in CEPA, more than 20 percent of the day's trade, said one broker.
Hopewell advanced HK$0.525 to HK$4.95, while CEPA jumped HK$1.85 to HK$17.95.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market, while utilities came under the most selling pressure of the day.
CITIC Pacific gained HK$0.40 to HK$36.60, after trading as high as HK$37.00. Cathay Pacific put on HK$0.05 to close at HK$12.75.
Hong Kong Telecom dropped HK$0.15 to HK$13.85, while Hongkong Electric lost HK$0.10 to HK$24.80. China Light was unchanged at HK$36.90.
